summary:
# PyTorch and MLX verification on the local Mac

2026-09-08; M5 Pro, 18 CPU cores, 20 GPU cores, 64 GiB unified memory. Production remains PyTorch 2.10.0. PyTorch 2.14.0 and MLX 0.32.2 were installed in an isolated environment under this directory. Supporting packages match the project lockfile.

## Matched float32 benchmark

Median seconds for 200 full-batch training updates; three warm trials per configuration.

| Backend | Batch 96 | Batch 768 |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| PyTorch 2.10 / MPS | 0.168 | 0.587 |
| PyTorch 2.14 / MPS | 0.178 | 0.579 |
| MLX 0.32.2 / full float32 | 0.183 | 0.654 |
| MLX 0.32.2 / compiled, full float32 | 0.141 | 0.493 |
| PyTorch 2.14 / CPU, 6 threads | 0.339 | 1.646 |

All implementations use shared exported starting weights, actual board encodings, legal masks, labels, the 1261-64-8100 ReLU MLP, mean masked cross-entropy, and Adam at learning rate 0.01, betas (0.9, 0.999), epsilon 1e-8, no weight decay, with bias correction enabled. MLX bias correction defaults to false, so it was explicitly enabled.

The 96-position batch is the real saved training split. Batch 768 repeats it eight times for throughput; it is not additional training evidence. Three trials share the same initialization and assess timing variation, not training-seed variation. GPU work is synchronized/materialized, and each step checks for finite loss. Warmup and compilation, interpreter startup, labeling, replay/encoding, validation, and serialization are excluded. Configurations ran sequentially in shuffled order; the full-precision MLX correction was a later sequential pass. Desktop load/temperature were not controlled. PyTorch used eager execution; MLX is reported both uncompiled and compiled. PyTorch compilation was not evaluated.

## Precision correction

MLX defaults may use reduced-precision float32 matrix multiplication on this hardware. The initial default-precision port missed the strict initial-logit comparison: maximum absolute error 0.000182554. Official documentation explains the behavior: https://ml-explore.github.io/mlx/build/html/usage/precision.html . The matched table uses MLX_ENABLE_TF32=0, set before process startup. run_full_precision.py records this setting. Default-precision runs remain in the raw artifacts as separate results.

## Correctness and compatibility

- Full-precision MLX initial logits, loss, gradients, and first Adam update passed atol=1e-5, rtol=1e-4 against CPU PyTorch. Observed maximum errors: logits 1.04e-7, loss 2.38e-7, gradients 4.66e-9, first-update weights 7.07e-7. See math-verification.json.
- All 42 retained timing trials finished with finite losses, exact training-label agreement, legal outputs, and 0/32 held-out teacher agreement. This reproduces memorization, not generalization.
- All 14 retained final parameter sets loaded into the existing PyTorch architecture on CPU and reproduced their saved predictions on 96 training and 32 validation positions. See export-verification.json. This checks parameter transfer, not an integrated MLX checkpoint format.
- PyTorch 2.14 passed 21 focused learning/data/encoding integration tests, including existing checkpoint reload, CLI, HTTP and arena coverage. Two existing dependency warnings remain. The first invocation failed to find the qi CLI because the isolated environment was absent from PATH; the corrected invocation passed. Full repository checks were not run, and this is not a completed dependency migration.
- Final weights/losses are not bitwise equal across frameworks or compilation modes. Passing the initial numerical checks does not promise identical optimization trajectories.

## Interpretation

- Batch 96: PyTorch 2.14 / 2.10 elapsed-time ratio 1.057; compiled full-precision MLX is 1.19x as fast as PyTorch 2.10, saving 26.8 ms per 200-step fit.
- Batch 768: PyTorch 2.14 / 2.10 elapsed-time ratio 0.986; compiled full-precision MLX is 1.19x as fast as PyTorch 2.10, saving 94.5 ms per 200-step fit.

No material speedup from the PyTorch upgrade for this workload. MLX compilation offers a modest warm-loop gain, but uncompiled MLX is slower. Recommendation: retain PyTorch and use its MPS backend for the next policy experiment; neither the upgrade nor a framework port is justified by speed alone at the current scale. Rebenchmark when the architecture or batch regime changes.

## Reproduction

Use the existing .venv for PyTorch 2.10; use venv/bin/python in this directory for PyTorch 2.14 and MLX. GPU execution requires Metal access outside the restricted sandbox.

```sh
.venv/bin/python artifacts/learning/framework-benchmark/run_all.py
.venv/bin/python artifacts/learning/framework-benchmark/run_full_precision.py
MLX_ENABLE_TF32=0 artifacts/learning/framework-benchmark/venv/bin/python artifacts/learning/framework-benchmark/verify_math.py
.venv/bin/python artifacts/learning/framework-benchmark/verify_exports.py
PATH="$PWD/artifacts/learning/framework-benchmark/venv/bin:$PATH" artifacts/learning/framework-benchmark/venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_learning.py src/qi/learning/test_data.py src/qi/players/policy/test_encoding.py -q
```

Production source, lockfile, and checkpoints were unchanged. Scripts, isolated dependencies and evidence are local ignored artifacts.
